title: Read the practices on the Practices tab of P&P
prompt:
Story: Read the practices on the Practices tab of P&P

- **Story**: XXX-read-practices-tab
- **Created**: 2026-11-08
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: choose "P&P" in the menu, press the "Practices" tab, and read the fourteen fixed practices of BWYN, which now come from the
  database that a migration filled.

## Story

As a team member, I want to open the Practices tab of the Principles & Practices page and read the practices that every BWYN team
follows, so that I know which practices are non-negotiable before I write a story or a decision, and I can trust that they are the same
for every project and cannot be changed from the application.

This story also moves the practices from a list written in the frontend to **fixed data in the database**: the two SQL scripts in the
Reference are Flyway migrations (one creates the tables, one loads the practices), they are executed, and the practices stay hardcoded
in them.

---

# The journey

| # | The user... | What they see |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | chooses "P&P" in the menu on the left | the page "Principles & Practices", with the tabs "Principles" (selected) and "Practices" (with a small lock) |
| 2 | presses "Practices" | a read-only note, and two groups: "Extreme Programming practices" (amber) and "Evolutionary architecture practices" (green) |
| 3 | reads | seven numbered practices in each group, with their labels, "In BWYN: ..." and, sometimes, a remark |
| 4 | leaves the page and comes back | the Principles tab is selected again |

---

## Before this story

The backend does not exist yet (the repository builds only the frontend). This story needs what the ADRs already ask for as enablers: the
Spring Boot application (ADR 0004), PostgreSQL and Flyway with Testcontainers (ADRs 0006 and 0008), Spring Data JPA with Hibernate set to
validate (ADR 0007), ArchUnit (ADR 0005) and OpenAPI (ADR 0010). It is the first story to use all of them together.

## Acceptance tests

Reaching the tab

- [ ] **Given** a project, **When** the user chooses "P&P" in the menu, **Then** the page is titled "Principles & Practices", with the
  description "The principles this team holds to, and the Extreme Programming and evolutionary architecture practices it follows.", and
  two tabs: "Principles" (selected) and "Practices" (with a small lock).
- [ ] **Given** the page, **When** the user presses "Practices", **Then** that tab is the selected one (`aria-selected`) and the content of
  the Principles tab is replaced by the practices.
- [ ] **Given** the keyboard, **Then** both tabs can be reached with Tab and chosen with Enter or Space, and a visible focus ring shows
  where the focus is.
- [ ] **Given** the user leaves the page and comes back, **Then** the Principles tab is selected again. The choice of tab is not remembered.

The tab

- [ ] **Given** the Practices tab, **Then** a note with a lock says "Read-only. These practices are part of BWYN and are the same for every
  project, so they cannot be edited or removed.", and there is no button to add, edit or remove anything.
- [ ] **Given** the tab, **Then** it shows two groups, in this order. "Extreme Programming practices" (amber panel, rule "Non-negotiable.
  The team MUST practise every one of them.") has seven numbered practices: Stories, Continuous integration, Ten-Minute Build, Pair
  programming, Incremental design, Single code base, Code review.
- [ ] **Given** the second group, "Evolutionary architecture practices" (green panel, rule "Applied through ADRs and architectural
  enablers. Architectural fitness functions are non-negotiable."), **Then** it has seven numbered practices: Build the skeleton first,
  Include automation early, Use architectural fitness functions, Defer reversible decisions, Grow incrementally, Design for testability,
  Align teams with Conway's law.
- [ ] **Given** a practice, **Then** it shows its number in its group, its name, a label with its group ("Extreme Programming" or
  "Evolutionary architecture"), what it is, a line "In BWYN: ..." saying how it shows up in the product, and, when there is one, a small
  italic remark.
- [ ] **Given** the practices, **Then** every Extreme Programming practice has a "Non-negotiable" label, and in the second group only "Use
  architectural fitness functions" has it: eight in all.
- [ ] **Given** the texts, **Then** each practice reads exactly as in the second script of the Reference: its name, what it is, "In BWYN"
  and its remark.

Where they come from

- [ ] **Given** the tab is opened, **Then** the browser asks the BWYN backend for the practices (`GET /api/practices`), and the page needs no
  model and no repository to show them.
- [ ] **Given** the answer has not arrived, **Then** the tab shows "Loading the practices..." under the note.
- [ ] **Given** the backend cannot be reached or answers with an error, **Then** the tab shows "The practices could not be loaded." with a
  "Try again" button, and the Principles tab is not affected. **When** the user presses it, **Then** the request is made again.
- [ ] **Given** two projects, **Then** both show the same practices, in the same order.
- [ ] **Given** the answer, **Then** the groups come in their order and the practices in their order inside each group, and no practice is
  repeated or missing.
- [ ] **Given** the backend, **Then** it offers no call to add, change or remove a practice: any other method on `/api/practices` is refused.

The database

- [ ] **Given** an empty PostgreSQL, **When** the application starts, **Then** Flyway runs the two migrations in order (the tables, then the
  practices), and the schema `practices` has two groups and fourteen practices, eight of them non-negotiable (seven of the first group
  and one of the second).
- [ ] **Given** the database, **Then** the order, the names, the texts, the "In BWYN" lines and the remarks in it are the ones of the
  second script, and the group of each practice is the right one.
- [ ] **Given** a started application, **When** it starts again, **Then** nothing changes in the practices and Flyway runs nothing.
- [ ] **Given** one of the migrations is edited after it was applied, **Then** Flyway's checksum check stops the application from
  starting.

## Business rules and constraints

- The practices are part of BWYN: the same for every project, never edited from the application, never removed. They are fixed data, and
  they are **hardcoded in Flyway migrations**: the two scripts in the Reference are those migrations, the first for the structure and the
  second for the data. No endpoint or screen writes them.
- A practice changes only through a **new migration** (an `UPDATE` or an `INSERT`). A merged migration is never edited (ADR 0006), so
  the history of the practices is the history of the migrations.
- The module `practices` owns the PostgreSQL schema `practices`. No other module reads or writes it directly: they ask for the practices
  through the module's public API (ADR 0006).
- Flyway creates the structure and the data. Hibernate only validates the mapping, and `data.sql` is not used (ADR 0007).
- The query side returns read models, never entities, and the call is described in the OpenAPI document (ADRs 0007 and 0010).
- A practice has a stable identity, a slug of its name (`continuous-integration`), so that anything that refers to it keeps its meaning.
- The answer of the backend has the same shape as the practices in the frontend today (group: `id`, `headline`, `badge`, `rule`; practice:
  `name`, `text`, `inBwyn`, `nonNegotiable`, `note`), with the identities added, so that the tab changes where it reads and not how it
  draws.
- For now the practices still reach the model and the repository from the list in the frontend (`practicesText()` and
  `practicesMarkdown()`), so the two lists must say the same until those two are moved too.

## Out of scope

- The Principles tab, and the Sync button next to the tabs, which keeps working as it does today (its own stories).
- Sending the practices to the model and writing `practices.md` from the database. They stay on the frontend's list until their own stories.
- Proposing, editing, translating, ordering or versioning practices, and a practice that belongs to one project.
- Choosing the PostgreSQL version, and the module layout of the rest of the backend.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Execute the scripts and hardcode the practices.** Put the two scripts of the Reference, as they are, in the migrations folder:
  `src/main/resources/db/migration/V202611081000__practices_create_tables.sql` and
  `src/main/resources/db/migration/V202611081001__practices_load_practices.sql`. Run them with Flyway on an empty PostgreSQL, once by
  starting the application and once in the integration test.
- [ ] Test the migrations against a real PostgreSQL started by Testcontainers: the schema, the two groups, the fourteen practices, the
  eight non-negotiable ones, the order, and the exact texts. A second start runs nothing.
- [ ] Add a test that compares the data of the migration with the list in `practices.ts` (name, text, "In BWYN", remark, non-negotiable, order),
  so that the two cannot drift until the model and the repository read from the database.
- [ ] Build the module `practices` with `domain`, `application` and `infrastructure`: a query port, a JPA mapping with the schema named
  (`@Table(schema = "practices")`), and an adapter that returns read models.
- [ ] Add the controller `GET /api/practices` that returns the groups with their practices, in order, with the Swagger annotations, and no
  other method.
- [ ] Test the adapter with an `*IT.java` against Testcontainers, and the controller with the OpenAPI document generated and checked.
- [ ] Make sure ArchUnit still passes with the new module.
- [ ] Add a client for the call in the frontend, and make the Practices tab read the groups from it, with "Loading the practices..." and
  "The practices could not be loaded." with "Try again".
- [ ] Take the list out of the tab component, and keep `practices.ts` only for `practicesText()` and `practicesMarkdown()`.

# Reference

## The scripts

PostgreSQL, in two Flyway migrations that run in this order. They follow ADR 0006: a version made of the date and time, then the module
and what the script does; the schema of the module; and explicit identifiers, because Hibernate creates nothing. The structure and the
data are apart, so that a later change to a practice is a small migration that touches data only. The data is the fixed list of
`practices.ts`, in its order.

### Script 1: `V202611081000__practices_create_tables.sql`

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA practices;

COMMENT ON SCHEMA practices IS 'Module practices: the fixed practices of the BWYN way of working.';

CREATE TABLE practices.practice_group (
    id            VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,
    display_order SMALLINT     NOT NULL,
    headline      VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    badge         VARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL,
    rule          VARCHAR(300) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_practice_group PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_practice_group_display_order UNIQUE (display_order)
);

CREATE TABLE practices.practice (
    id             VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    group_id       VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,
    display_order  SMALLINT     NOT NULL,
    name           VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    description    TEXT         NOT NULL,
    in_bwyn        TEXT         NOT NULL,
    non_negotiable BOOLEAN      NOT NULL,
    note           TEXT,
    CONSTRAINT pk_practice PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_practice_group FOREIGN KEY (group_id) REFERENCES practices.practice_group (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_practice_group_order UNIQUE (group_id, display_order)
);

COMMENT ON TABLE practices.practice_group IS 'Fixed reference data. The same for every project. Changed only by a new migration.';
COMMENT ON TABLE practices.practice IS 'Fixed reference data. The same for every project. Changed only by a new migration.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN practices.practice.in_bwyn IS 'How the practice shows up in BWYN.';
```
